excerpt: Shrink large JSON tool results for LLM agents without silently losing data. Package: agent-tool-result-reducer · Import: tool_result_reducer A zero-dependency Python library that fits an API/tool response into a character budget by selecting fields, dropping the widest fields, and cutting only on whole-item boundaries — and that always tells the model, in a _meta block, exactly what it did and did not receive. Before: [{"id":1,"name":"Acme","description":"…"},{"id":2,"name":"content delivery networ ← cut mid-object After: {"items":[…25 whole items…],"_meta":{"items_included":25,"items_available":25, "total_reported_by_source":443,"fields_dropped":{"description":3617},…}} pip install agent-tool-result-reducer Requires Python 3.10+. No runtime dependencies. from tool_result_reducer import reduce_tool_result rows = [{"id": i, "name": f"Company {i}", "description": "long text " * 400} for i in range(25)] response = {"results": rows, "total": 443} # a page of 25 companies, about 100,000 characters result = reduce_tool_result(response, "crm.search", budget=4_000) result.text # 1,506 characters of valid JSON: this is what goes to the model result.complete # True: all 25 items are there; the wide `description` field was dropped result.summary("crm.search") # crm.search: complete, agent received 25 of 25 items (source reports 443 in total), dropped fields: description The model is told what happened, in the result itself: "_meta": {"items_included": 25, "items_available": 25, "complete": true, "total_reported_by_source": 443, "total_note": "`complete` covers this response only. The source reports 443 in total; ...", "fields_dropped": {"description": 4017}, ...} Give agent builders a drop-in function that sits between "tool returned something" and "append it to the model's context", so that: - A result fits the budget you set, short of cutting a single item in half (cost and context-window control). - What the model receives is always valid JSON made of whole items. - When…
